title: Yara and the Deadline
premise: Yara Vance, a burned intelligence handler living under a polished lie, receives a calendar invite from her mentor — sent after his death — summoning her to a meeting she cannot refuse. There she collides with Cyrus Coldharbour, a crash investigator obsessed with the aviation disaster that killed his family in row twelve, and discovers the crash was no accident but a covered-up assassination tied to a secret worth killing for: proof of who ordered it. Hunted by the agency that trained them both, Yara and Cyrus must decide whether to trade the evidence for their own survival or burn their handlers publicly, even as their wary alliance deepens into love that duty forbids. In the end Yara releases the truth at devastating personal cost, finds belonging not in an institution but in the family she builds with Cyrus, and walks away from the law to deliver justice on her own terms.
about_author: Sebastian Reyes is a former airline safety analyst turned novelist who writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside institutional lies. He lives in Lisbon, where he claims the best plot ideas arrive during turbulence.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag by the Door
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. We meet her in her carefully constructed life: fake name, packed bag, nightly ritual of checking exits. A flashback hints at the operation that went wrong and the mentor, Aldous Wren, who taught her to lie beautifully. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness, the cost of always being ready to run.

chapters.title: Invitation from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A calendar ping arrives from Wren's account — scheduled before his 'suicide,' set for tomorrow, 9 a.m., Terminal C. She verifies he's truly dead, then finds a hidden cipher in the invite body only she could read. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into compulsion; grief weaponized.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Introduce Cyrus at the crash site memorial, five years on, still cataloguing inconsistencies in Flight 4471's wreckage report. His daughter's seat was row twelve. He receives an anonymous tip naming Wren. Emotional beat: obsession as devotion; grief that refuses closure.

chapters.title: Terminal C, Nine O'Clock
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Both arrive at the meeting spot; instead of Wren, they find a dead courier and a live ambush. Forced together mid-firefight, they escape using complementary skills — hers tradecraft, his forensic precision. Emotional beat: adrenaline-fused distrust between strangers.

chapters.title: What the Courier Carried
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Examining the courier's effects, Cyrus identifies a data shard matching serial numbers from his crash investigation. Yara recognizes the encryption as agency work. They realize Wren was building a case against their own employers. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forming over shared enemies.

chapters.title: The Lie She Polished
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Interrogated by memory: what Wren knew about her past, why she defected, what the shard might expose about her own complicity. She hides one file from Cyrus. Emotional beat: guilt; love against duty begins its first quiet test.

chapters.title: Safehouse Rules
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Holed up in a derelict canal house, they establish rules: no real names, no pasts. The rules erode within hours as Cyrus's forensic mind and Yara's tradecraft interlock. Emotional beat: intimacy growing inside enforced secrecy.

chapters.title: The Handler Who Wouldn't Stay Dead
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Evidence suggests Wren may have staged his death — or someone wanted him erased posthumously. A burner call plays his voice: 'Trade it or bury it, Yara. Not both.' Emotional beat: hope curdling into manipulation; is the message real?

chapters.title: Men from the Ministry
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Agency cleaners raid Cyrus's apartment; his neighbor is questioned, his sister threatened. He realizes protecting Yara means painting a target on everyone he has left. Emotional beat: rage and protectiveness; stakes turn personal again.

chapters.title: Decoding Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The shard decrypts partially: flight telemetry altered, a passenger list redacted — except row twelve, flagged for extraction that never happened. Cyrus learns his family may have been collateral in a hit meant for one man. Emotional beat: devastation transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The One Secret Worth Killing For
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Full decryption reveals the order came from inside the agency's oversight council — and Yara's old unit ran the ground team. Her hidden file surfaces; Cyrus confronts her. Emotional beat: betrayal, confession, the fragile question of forgiveness.

chapters.title: Midnight on the Canal
chapters.summary: Both POVs. After the fight, a raw conversation: he mourns aloud for the first time; she tells the whole truth of her defection. Neither sleeps. Emotional beat: love acknowledged against every rule they wrote.

chapters.title: Auction Notice
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The council leaks word that the shard's existence is known; a buyer — a foreign syndicate — offers sanctuary for the evidence. Wren's voice returns via dead-drop: take the trade. Emotional beat: temptation; justice versus survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Sister in Bruges
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus moves his sister to safety and finds her already surveilled — the council is closing nets. He chooses openly now: Yara, the mission, the truth. Emotional beat: duty inverted; family redefined by choice.

chapters.title: Trap at the Exchange
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The syndicate meeting is a joint council-syndicate sting. Yara and Cyrus walk in knowing it, carrying a decoy shard, and fight out through a flooded freight yard. Emotional beat: trust proven under fire; no more half-measures.

chapters.title: Wren's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. They trace Wren's final dead-drop to a boat on the estuary — alive, dying, hiding. He confesses he scheduled the invite to force her hand, believing she'd trade the secret and survive. He gives them the council's meeting ledger. Emotional beat: grief for a mentor who loved her the only way he could.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The council convenes in Geneva in under a day to ratify the cover-up permanently. Yara and Cyrus plan an impossible broadcast: breach the secure archive, mirror the evidence globally before capture. Emotional beat: cold clarity; fear converted into resolve.

chapters.title: Geneva, Locked Doors
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Infiltration through service tunnels while Yara poses as a delegate's aide. Near-discovery forces improvisation; Cyrus reaches the archive node as alarms trip. Emotional beat: terror held at bay by discipline and devotion.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Climax. The evidence floods every feed: flight telemetry, the kill order, the council's signatures. Capture teams close in; Yara stays behind to hold the upload, trading herself for Cyrus's escape window. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the purest form of justice outside the law.

chapters.title: What the World Does with Truth
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Detained and interrogated, Yara watches the scandal detonate anyway — resignations, arrests, hearings. Cyrus works the outside, leaking her location to journalists until detention becomes untenable. Emotional beat: vindication without triumph; the machine bleeds but stands.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Released, stateless, formally erased — and free. Cyrus meets her at a small coastal cemetery where row twelve's names are finally being corrected on the memorial. Emotional beat: mourning completed; two broken people choosing each other.

chapters.title: No More Deadlines
chapters.summary: Both POVs, closing. Months later: a new town, a door with no go-bag beside it. An encrypted message arrives — old colleagues, new trouble — and they read it together, then let it go. Emotional beat: peace earned, vigilance softened into hope; the arc closes on belonging.
